intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the aurora borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to maximize your viewing experience, often venturing to remote highland locations.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy the signature silica mud mask, in-water bar service, and steam caves while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for a well-rounded experience within budget.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and small geysers in a stunning rural setting, offering a more local and intimate experience.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and cultural landmarks on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs at iconic spots like Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church and the colorful old harbor district.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's breathtaking rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve and reward yourself with a soak in the natural geothermal hot spring pool at Landmannalaugar. The hike offers surreal landscapes of obsidian lava fields, steaming vents, and vivid multicolored mountains unlike anywhere else on Earth.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Travel Day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Travel Day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (~3,000 ISK) to Reykjavik. Check into Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a quick snack from a nearby convenience store or 24-hour gas station (N1 or Orkan) to save money. Rest and prepare for the adventure ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit or airport meal
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from convenience store or gas station (skyr, sandwich, hot dog ~500-800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Iceland's famous pylsur (hot dogs) at gas stations are a beloved budget staple. Keep receipts for tax refund eligibility. January temperatures average -1°C to 3°C, so layer up immediately upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a slow morning at the hotel. Walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort and take in the dramatic Icelandic winter coastline. Watch for seabirds and enjoy the moody January atmosphere. Pick up groceries from a nearby Bonus or Kronan supermarket (cheapest chains in Iceland) to stock up on budget breakfast supplies like skyr, bread, and fruit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Hallgrimskirkja Church (free to view exterior, ~1,000 ISK to take the elevator to the top for panoramic city views). Stroll down Skolavordustigur street lined with colorful shops. Walk to the old harbor area (Grandi) and explore the free outdoor areas. Visit the Sun Voyager sculpture along the waterfront — free and photogenic.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the hotel for sunset (around 16:30 in January). After dark, check the Icelandic Met Office aurora forecast (vedur.is) and the Aurora app for northern lights activity. If KP index is favorable, bundle up and head to a dark spot near the beachfront or a low-light area outside the city for your first northern lights attempt.

meals.breakfast: Skyr and fruit from supermarket (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Baejarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog stand near harbor — Iceland's most famous hot dog (~500 ISK each)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or soup from supermarket ingredients (~800-1,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January offers some of the best northern lights viewing conditions due to long dark nights (up to 19 hours of darkness). Download the Vedur app for real-time aurora alerts. Always check road conditions at road.is before venturing out.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and head to the famous Blue Lagoon area — however, to save money, skip the expensive Blue Lagoon (entry ~15,000+ ISK) and instead visit the nearby Grindavik area for coastal walks and dramatic lava field scenery, which is completely free. Alternatively, visit Seltjarnarnes Peninsula just west of Reykjavik for a free, stunning coastal walk with lighthouse views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a bus to the Reykjanes Peninsula. Explore the Bridge Between Continents (free) — a small bridge spanning the Mid-Atlantic Ridge where the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates meet. Visit Reykjanesviti Lighthouse (free) and the dramatic geothermal area at Gunnuhver hot springs (free to walk around). Marvel at the bubbling mud pools and steam vents.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Monitor northern lights forecast. If aurora activity is predicted, drive or join a free/low-cost aurora walking tour from Reykjavik city center. Many hostels and guesthouses organize free aurora alerts for guests. Try the beachfront near the hotel for dark-sky viewing.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal and coffee prepared at hotel (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed sandwiches from supermarket enjoyed at Reykjanes Peninsula (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hlolla Baer burger restaurant in Reykjavik — affordable Icelandic fast food (~2,000-2,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Gunnuhver hot springs area was significantly affected by recent volcanic activity near Grindavik — always check current access and safety conditions at safetravel.is before visiting Reykjanes Peninsula. Dress in waterproof layers as geothermal steam can be wet.

day_by_day.morning: Start the famous Golden Circle route early. Drive to Thingvellir National Park (free entry, small parking fee ~750 ISK). This UNESCO World Heritage Site is where Iceland's first parliament was established in 930 AD. Walk the Almannagjá gorge between tectonic plates — one of Iceland's most dramatic free natural attractions. Allow 2 hours to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area (free entry). Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes, shooting boiling water up to 30 meters high. Walk the surrounding geothermal field carefully on marked paths. Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall (free entry) — one of Iceland's most powerful and beautiful waterfalls. The winter ice formations make it especially magical.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik or find a dark rural pullout along Route 35 for northern lights watching on the way home. The Golden Circle route offers excellent dark-sky conditions far from city light pollution. Return to hotel and warm up with hot drinks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or supermarket yogurt and granola (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket eaten at Geysir or Gullfoss (~700 ISK). Avoid the expensive tourist cafes at these sites.
meals.dinner: Supermarket ready meal or self-cooked dinner at hotel (~1,000-1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300km round trip from Reykjavik. Renting a small car split between travelers is often cheaper than a tour bus (~8,000-12,000 ISK/day for car rental). January roads can be icy — ensure you have a 4WD or winter tires. Check road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjavik Settlement Museum (Landnamssyning) — entry ~2,500 ISK — to learn about Iceland's Viking history built around actual 10th-century ruins discovered beneath the city. Alternatively, visit the National Museum of Iceland (~2,500 ISK) for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Grandi Harbor District — Reykjavik's hip waterfront neighborhood. Visit the free Reykjavik Maritime Museum exterior and harbor area. Browse the Kolaportid flea market (open weekends, small entry fee ~200 ISK) for secondhand goods and local food stalls selling traditional Icelandic foods like hardfiskur (dried fish) and kleinur pastries. Walk along the harbor and watch for seals.
day_by_day.evening: Budget hot spring experience: Visit Vesturbaejarlaug or Sundholl Reykjavik — public swimming pools with geothermal hot tubs (entry ~1,100 ISK). These are where locals actually go and offer the authentic hot spring experience at a fraction of commercial spa prices. Soak in the hot pots while potentially watching northern lights overhead if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Skyr with berries from supermarket (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Snacks from Kolaportid flea market — try hardfiskur and traditional pastries (~800-1,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Noodle Station — Reykjavik's beloved budget noodle soup restaurant, a favorite among locals (~1,800-2,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Icelandic public pools (sundlaugar) are a cultural institution and the best budget hot spring experience available. Bring flip flops and follow the mandatory shower-before-entering rules. Most pools have multiple hot tubs at different temperatures. This is a must-do cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hveragerdi — Iceland's geothermal garden town, about 45 minutes east of Reykjavik on Route 1. Visit the NLFI Geothermal Park in town center (small fee ~1,000 ISK) with indoor geysers and hot springs. The town itself is built over intense geothermal activity with steam rising from gardens and streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Reykjadalur Hot Spring River trail from Hveragerdi — a free 3km hike (each way) through geothermal landscape leading to a naturally hot river where you can bathe for free. This is one of Iceland's best free hot spring experiences. The hike takes about 45-60 minutes each way. Bring a swimsuit and towel. The trail can be icy in January — use hiking poles or microspikes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Warm up at the hotel. Check aurora forecast — if activity is high (KP 3+), drive to a dark area outside the city. The area around Thingvellir or even the coast near the hotel can offer good viewing. Many nights in January offer multiple aurora sightings.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or supermarket oatmeal with honey (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed thermos of hot soup and sandwiches to enjoy at the hot river — essential for warmth (~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Kebab or pizza from a budget restaurant in Reykjavik (~1,500-2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hike is one of Iceland's best free experiences but can be challenging in January due to ice and darkness. Start early to maximize the limited daylight (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~16:30). Wear waterproof hiking boots and bring a change of clothes for after the hot river swim. The water temperature varies — find a comfortable spot.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day and mid-trip recovery. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning. Visit the Reykjavik Botanical Garden (Grasagardur) — free entry, beautiful even in winter with frosted plants and occasional snow. Walk through Miklatun Park nearby. Visit a local cafe for a warming coffee and pastry — try Sandholt Bakery for fresh Icelandic bread and pastries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Tjornin Pond in central Reykjavik — free and beautiful, often partially frozen in January with ducks and swans. Walk to the Austurvollur square and Althingi (Icelandic Parliament) building. Browse the independent shops along Laugavegur street — window shopping is free. Visit the Einar Jonsson Sculpture Garden (free outdoor garden) next to Hallgrimskirkja.
day_by_day.evening: Visit another public geothermal pool — try Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest public pool complex (~1,100 ISK). It has multiple hot tubs, a steam room, and a large outdoor pool. Perfect for relaxing tired muscles. Afterward, enjoy a budget dinner and prepare gear for the second week of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread and coffee from Sandholt Bakery (~1,200 ISK — a slight splurge for quality)
meals.lunch: Self-made sandwiches from supermarket (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Supermarket self-catering — make a traditional Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) using supermarket ingredients (~1,200 ISK for a full pot)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest days are important in Iceland's winter conditions. Use this day to do laundry if needed (many guesthouses have laundry facilities for ~500-1,000 ISK). Review your aurora viewing attempts so far and plan dedicated late-night aurora hunts for the remaining days based on forecast patterns.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the South Coast drive — one of Iceland's most dramatic routes. Head east on Route 1. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall (free, small parking fee ~750 ISK). In summer you can walk behind it, but in January the path behind may be icy and closed — check conditions. The frozen or partially frozen waterfall in winter is extraordinarily beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skogafoss waterfall (free, parking fee ~750 ISK) — another massive, powerful waterfall. Climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views over the South Coast. In January, the surrounding cliffs are often draped in ice and icicles. Continue toward Vik — Iceland's southernmost village. Stop at Dyrholaey Peninsula viewpoint (may be closed in winter storms — check conditions) for views of black sand beaches and sea stacks.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Vik village. Walk to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach (free) — one of the world's most famous black sand beaches with dramatic basalt columns and the Reynisdrangar sea stacks. WARNING: Never turn your back on the ocean — sneaker waves are extremely dangerous year-round. Watch for northern lights from the beach if skies clear. Stay overnight in Vik at a budget guesthouse (~6,000-9,000 ISK) or return to Reykjavik.

meals.breakfast: Early supermarket breakfast before departing (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Skogafoss (~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Sudur-Vik restaurant in Vik village — reasonably priced by Icelandic standards (~3,000-3,500 ISK) or supermarket/gas station meal (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast drive is approximately 180km one way from Reykjavik to Vik. Daylight is precious in January — depart by 9:00 AM to maximize the ~5.5 hours of usable daylight. Road conditions can change rapidly; always check road.is. Reynisfjara beach has claimed lives — respect the warning signs and never approach the waterline.

day_by_day.morning: If staying in Vik, wake up early for a sunrise walk on Reynisfjara Beach (sunrise ~11:00 in January). The low winter sun creates incredible golden light on the black sand and basalt columns. Drive further east to Vatnajokull National Park area. Stop at Fjadrargljufur Canyon (check if accessible in winter — sometimes closed) — a stunning, ancient canyon carved by glacial rivers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jokulsarlon Glacier Lagoon (free to view, ~280km from Reykjavik). This iconic lagoon filled with floating blue icebergs calved from Breidamerkurjokull glacier is one of Iceland's most spectacular sights. Walk to the nearby Diamond Beach where icebergs wash up on black sand — completely free and utterly magical. In January, the lagoon may be partially frozen, adding to the otherworldly atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: This is prime northern lights territory — far from any city light pollution. The area around Jokulsarlon is one of Iceland's best aurora viewing spots. If KP index allows, stay until dark (which comes early — around 16:30) and watch for the aurora over the glacier lagoon — a once-in-a-lifetime potential photo opportunity. Begin the long drive back toward Reykjavik or stay at a budget guesthouse in the area.

meals.breakfast: Gas station breakfast in Vik or packed food (~800 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Diamond Beach (~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Gas station hot food or self-catered meal (~1,200-1,800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Jokulsarlon is approximately 375km from Reykjavik — this is a very long day. Consider staying 1-2 nights in the area rather than doing it as a day trip. The drive along Route 1 in January requires full concentration — ice, snow, and darkness are common. A 4WD vehicle is strongly recommended for this route. Fill up on fuel whenever possible as gas stations are sparse in the east.

day_by_day.morning: Return journey toward Reykjavik along the South Coast (if you drove east yesterday). Stop at Skaftafell area within Vatnajokull National Park for a free walk through the birch forest — beautiful with frost and snow in January. Visit the free visitor center to learn about the park and glacier geology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Kirkjubaejarklaustur village (known as Klaustur) — a small community with interesting geological features. Visit Kirkjugolf (Church Floor) — a natural basalt column formation resembling a tiled floor, free to visit. Continue west and stop again at Skogafoss or Seljalandsfoss if you missed them on the way east. Arrive back in Reykjavik by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel. Visit a public geothermal pool for a soak. Check aurora forecast for a late-night viewing session. By now you should have a good feel for aurora patterns — January 2027 is expected to be near solar maximum, offering excellent aurora activity.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or packed food (~600 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the road (~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at Reykjavik — try Aktu Taktu fast food restaurant, a local chain with affordable burgers and fish (~1,800-2,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: If you find the long South Coast drive too exhausting for one day, consider splitting Day 8-10 differently. The South Coast and Jokulsarlon can easily fill 2-3 dedicated days. Adjust the itinerary based on your energy levels and road conditions encountered.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Snæfellsnes Peninsula — a 2-3 hour drive north from Reykjavik. This magical peninsula is home to the Snæfellsjokull glacier volcano (immortalized in Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth). Drive along the south coast of the peninsula, stopping at Arnarstapi fishing village with its dramatic coastal cliffs and rock formations — free to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the peninsula to Kirkjufell mountain — Iceland's most photographed mountain, located near Grundarfjordur village. The mountain is particularly stunning in winter with snow and ice. The nearby Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall is free to visit and creates a classic Icelandic composition. Continue to Stykkisholmur town for a walk around the charming harbor and lighthouse hill (free).
day_by_day.evening: The Snæfellsnes Peninsula offers excellent northern lights viewing with minimal light pollution. If aurora activity is forecast, stay in the area until dark and watch from the coast. Drive back to Reykjavik (or stay overnight in Stykkisholmur at a budget guesthouse ~6,000-8,000 ISK).

meals.breakfast: Early supermarket breakfast before departure (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Kirkjufell (~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Narfeyrarstofa restaurant in Stykkisholmur for local fish soup (~2,500-3,000 ISK) or gas station meal (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is called 'Iceland in Miniature' because it contains almost every type of Icelandic landscape. The round trip from Reykjavik is approximately 350km. Check weather forecasts specifically for the peninsula — it can have dramatically different weather from Reykjavik. The Snæfellsjokull glacier summit is not accessible in winter without a guided tour.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated northern lights morning prep day. Sleep in after any late-night aurora chasing. Visit the Aurora Reykjavik museum (~2,000 ISK) — an excellent interactive museum about the science and mythology of the northern lights, great for understanding what you've been seeing. Browse the Laugavegur shopping street for last-minute souvenirs — look for budget options like Icelandic wool socks, small lava stone items, or locally produced chocolates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Oskjuhlid Hill — free, and home to the Perlan building (the distinctive dome structure). Walk the free forest trails around the hill. The Perlan has a free observation deck offering 360-degree views over Reykjavik. Visit the Nauthólsvík Geothermal Beach — a small sandy beach with geothermally heated seawater (entry ~900 ISK in winter). It's a unique experience to swim in warm water on a black sand beach in January.
day_by_day.evening: DEDICATED AURORA NIGHT: This is your penultimate evening — make it count. Book a budget aurora minibus tour (~5,000-8,000 ISK) that drives to the darkest available skies based on real-time cloud cover. These tours include expert guides and often provide hot chocolate. Alternatively, rent a car and drive to Thingvellir or the Reykjanes Peninsula independently for dark-sky viewing. Stay out until midnight if aurora activity is present.

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast — skyr and granola at hotel (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch at Reykjavik — try Icelandic Fish and Chips at Grandi (~2,200 ISK) for a local specialty
meals.dinner: Early dinner before aurora hunting — supermarket meal prep (~1,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January 2027 is expected to be near or at solar maximum (Solar Cycle 25 peak), making it one of the best years in over a decade for northern lights viewing. Even with moderate KP index (2-3), auroras can be visible in Iceland's dark winter skies. The key factors are clear skies and darkness — always prioritize cloud-free areas over staying in one spot.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Pack and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. If time allows before airport transfer, take a final walk along the beachfront to soak in the Icelandic landscape one last time. Visit a local bakery for a farewell pastry and coffee. Pick up any last souvenirs — Bonus supermarket has affordable Icelandic products like skyr, licorice, and local sweets to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, consider a final stop at a public geothermal pool for one last hot soak — the perfect way to end an Icelandic trip. Take the Flybus shuttle back to Keflavik Airport (~3,000 ISK). Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security. Claim your VAT tax refund at the airport (on purchases over 6,000 ISK from participating stores).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with incredible memories of northern lights, hot springs, dramatic landscapes, and Viking history. The 13 days in Iceland's winter wonderland will have provided some of the most unique travel experiences possible on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Final Icelandic breakfast — fresh pastry from local bakery (~1,000-1,200 ISK)
meals.lunch: Airport meal or final gas station hot dog as a farewell Icelandic tradition (~800-1,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant

day_by_day.notes: BUDGET SUMMARY ESTIMATE: Accommodation (12 nights at budget level): ~72,000-96,000 ISK. Food (self-catering + budget restaurants): ~60,000-80,000 ISK. Transportation (car rental + fuel or buses): ~40,000-60,000 ISK. Activities and entrance fees: ~20,000-30,000 ISK. Airport transfers: ~6,000 ISK. TOTAL ESTIMATE: ~198,000-272,000 ISK (~$1,400-$1,950 USD) for the 13 days excluding flights. Key money-saving tips: shop at Bonus/Kronan supermarkets, use public pools instead of commercial spas, prioritize free natural attractions, and split car rental costs with fellow travelers.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and collect baggage. Take the Flybus or arrange a pre-booked airport transfer (~45 min) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room. Step outside briefly to scan the sky for northern lights if energy permits — January skies in Iceland offer long dark hours perfect for aurora spotting.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In flight
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack at Keflavik Airport upon arrival (Icelandic lamb soup or a sandwich at the terminal café) before heading to the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance. January in Iceland means near-total darkness by late afternoon — dress in warm, waterproof layers immediately upon landing. Temperatures can be -2°C to 4°C. Keep your aurora alert app (such as Vedur.is) active from night one.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. After breakfast, take a gentle orientation stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Breathe in the crisp Arctic air and get your bearings. Visit a nearby local geothermal pool or hot pot if available near the resort for a relaxing warm soak to reset your body clock.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Reykjavik (approx. 30–50 min depending on resort location) for the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour. Explore the colorful streets of the city, visit Hallgrímskirkja Church, the Sun Voyager sculpture, and sample traditional Icelandic bites including skyr, lamb soup, fermented shark (hákarl), and fresh bread. Learn about Viking history and Icelandic culture from your local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area for dinner. Check aurora forecast for tonight — if KP index is favorable, head to a dark spot near the resort for your first Northern Lights attempt. January darkness begins around 16:00, giving maximum viewing windows.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — skyr with berries, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs, and Icelandic coffee.
meals.lunch: During the walking tour, sample street food and café stops included in the tour experience — try a bowl of lamb soup at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja (~2,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Dine at a mid-range Reykjavik restaurant such as Grillmarkaðurinn (Grillmarket) or Snaps Bistro — budget ~5,000–7,000 ISK per person for Icelandic fish or lamb dishes.

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour typically runs 2–3 hours. Book in advance for January as group sizes are smaller. Wear sturdy waterproof boots as Reykjavik streets can be icy in January.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — one of Iceland's most iconic experiences. The Blue Lagoon is conveniently located near Keflavik Airport and easily reachable from the resort. Book the Comfort Package (includes silica mud mask, algae mask, and a drink). Arrive early for the 08:00 or 09:00 slot to enjoy the steaming milky-blue 38–40°C waters before crowds build. The contrast of warm water against cold January air and possible snowfall is magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Blue Lagoon, head back toward the resort or explore the Reykjanes Peninsula. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (a small footbridge spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates) and the Reykjanes Lighthouse — both free and stunning in winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — join a guided super jeep evening tour departing from the Reykjavik area. Expert guides use real-time aurora forecasts and cloud cover data to drive you away from light pollution into optimal viewing zones. Tours typically run 21:00–01:00. Wrap up in provided blankets and enjoy hot cocoa under the dancing lights.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before departing early for Blue Lagoon.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Blue Lagoon's LAVA Restaurant or the in-lagoon swim-up bar — try the Icelandic fish tacos or soup (~3,500–5,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Early dinner at a casual spot near the resort or a packed thermos of hot soup from the resort for the Super Jeep tour — many tours provide light snacks onboard.

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon must be pre-booked online — slots sell out weeks in advance even in January. Bring a hair tie as the silica-rich water can tangle hair. The Super Jeep Northern Lights tour typically costs 12,000–15,000 ISK per person — confirm pickup location from your resort.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the late-night aurora tour. Sleep in, have a slow breakfast. Spend the morning reviewing photos and journaling. If energy allows, take a short walk along the beachfront — January coastal scenery in Iceland is dramatic with dark skies, crashing waves, and potential frost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a guided tour along the famous Golden Circle route — visit Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site, where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet), the Geysir Geothermal Area (watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes), and Gullfoss Waterfall (partially frozen in January, spectacular). The full loop takes about 6–8 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby local eatery. Check aurora forecast — if clear skies, step outside for a spontaneous viewing session from the resort grounds.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort — take your time.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the resort or stop at the Geysir Center café for lamb soup and fresh Icelandic bread (~2,000–3,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant — try the pan-seared Arctic char or slow-roasted lamb shank (~5,000–6,500 ISK per person).

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle roads are generally well-maintained but can be icy in January. Consider renting a 4WD vehicle or joining a guided Golden Circle tour (~9,000–12,000 ISK per person). Daylight in January is limited to roughly 10:00–16:00 — plan accordingly to see all three stops in daylight.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891. The drive from the Reykjavik/resort area takes about 1.5 hours. Arrive early to enjoy the natural hot spring pool (~38–40°C) surrounded by geothermal steam vents and a small geyser that erupts periodically. Far less commercial than the Blue Lagoon, this is a deeply authentic Icelandic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Secret Lagoon, explore the charming village of Flúðir and nearby geothermal greenhouses where Icelanders grow tomatoes and cucumbers year-round using geothermal energy. Drive back toward the resort, stopping at the Kerið Volcanic Crater Lake — a stunning crimson and teal crater accessible year-round (~400 ISK entry fee).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a quiet evening with a hot drink by the fire. If aurora conditions are favorable (check Vedur.is), head to the beach or a dark area near the resort for viewing. January offers some of the best aurora probability of the year.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before the early departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Secret Lagoon's small on-site café or a packed lunch — try local Icelandic flatbread (flatbrauð) with smoked lamb.
meals.dinner: Cook-your-own or order in — visit a local Bonus supermarket (Iceland's budget-friendly chain) and pick up Icelandic ingredients for a simple self-catered dinner if your room has kitchen facilities, or dine at the resort (~4,500–6,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry is approximately 3,200 ISK per adult. Book online in advance. The road to Flúðir is paved but check road conditions on road.is before departing. Bring your own towel or rent one at the lagoon.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning for rest and resort enjoyment. Take advantage of any resort amenities — spa, pool, or lounge. Browse local Icelandic handicrafts at nearby shops. Consider a short morning yoga or meditation session on the beachfront if weather permits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approx. 2–2.5 hours from Reykjavik). Visit the iconic Snæfellsjökull Glacier and National Park — immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth.' Stop at Arnarstapi cliffs, Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach, and the charming fishing village of Grundarfjörður with views of Kirkjufell mountain (the 'arrowhead mountain' from Game of Thrones).
day_by_day.evening: Kirkjufell mountain at dusk is a prime northern lights photography location. If aurora activity is predicted, stay in the Grundarfjörður area into the evening for an incredible backdrop of lights over the iconic mountain before driving back. Return to resort late evening.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Narfeyrarstofa restaurant in Stykkishólmur or a packed lunch — try fresh Icelandic scallops or fish soup (~3,000–4,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Early dinner in Grundarfjörður at Bjargarsteinn Mathús (a beloved local restaurant) before aurora hunting — try the fish of the day (~4,500–6,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a full-day trip. Start no later than 09:00 to maximize the limited daylight. Road conditions on the peninsula can be challenging in January — 4WD strongly recommended. This is one of Iceland's most scenic and underrated destinations.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day — midpoint of the trip. Sleep in and enjoy a long, leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning reading, relaxing in the resort spa, or soaking in any on-site hot tub with ocean views. Reflect on the first half of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Reykjavik for a cultural afternoon. Explore the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) — excellent exhibits on Viking-age artifacts and Icelandic history (~2,000 ISK entry). Stroll Laugavegur Street for window shopping and local boutiques. Stop at a cozy café for Icelandic kleinur (twisted doughnuts) and coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — book a second tour for tonight to maximize your aurora chances. January is peak aurora season with up to 18 hours of darkness. Experienced guides will chase clear skies across the region. Return late to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Extended resort breakfast — try the Icelandic skyr pancakes.
meals.lunch: Cozy café lunch in Reykjavik — try Café Babalu or Stofan Café for homemade soups and open-faced sandwiches (~2,000–3,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Pre-tour dinner at Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavik — a celebrated mid-range restaurant specializing in traditional Icelandic recipes reimagined (~5,500–7,500 ISK per person).

day_by_day.notes: This is a strategic rest and recovery day before the more active second half of the trip. The second Super Jeep aurora tour increases your chances significantly — January cloud cover can be unpredictable so two attempts are highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the South Coast — one of Iceland's most dramatic driving routes. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall, where you can walk behind the curtain of water (may be partially icy in January — exercise caution). Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall — climb the 527 steps to the top for panoramic winter views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach near Vík — one of the world's most famous black beaches. Admire the towering basalt columns, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. Exercise extreme caution — sneaker waves are deadly here year-round. Visit the charming village of Vík í Mýrdal and the red-roofed church on the hill.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a guesthouse or hotel near Vík for the night (pre-booked mid-range accommodation ~15,000–20,000 ISK) or return to Aegean Bliss Resort (approx. 2.5 hours). If staying near Vík, the dark skies offer excellent aurora viewing away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from the resort or a quick stop at a petrol station bakery en route.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skógarfoss area — the Skógafoss Guesthouse café serves warm soups and sandwiches (~2,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Halldórskaffi in Vík — a beloved local restaurant with Icelandic lamb stew and fresh fish (~4,500–6,000 ISK per person).

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast is approximately 2.5–3 hours from Reykjavik. This can be done as a long day trip or with an overnight stay. January road conditions on Route 1 are generally manageable but check road.is daily. Daylight window is narrow — prioritize Seljalandsfoss and Skógafoss in the morning light.

day_by_day.morning: If overnighting near Vík — morning visit to the Dyrhólaey Peninsula for dramatic sea arch views and potential puffin sightings (rare in January but the landscape is stunning). Drive to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (approx. 2 hours east of Vík) — one of Iceland's most breathtaking sights. Watch enormous blue icebergs calve from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier and float serenely in the lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Diamond Beach directly across the road from Jökulsárlón — where translucent ice chunks wash up on black sand like scattered diamonds. Spend time photographing this otherworldly landscape. Visit the nearby Fjallsárlón Glacier Lagoon for a quieter, equally beautiful alternative. Begin the return drive westward.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort (approx. 4–5 hour drive from Jökulsárlón). Stop at Kirkjubæjarklaustur village for a warm meal on the way back. Arrive at the resort by 21:00–22:00. Rest and recharge.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Vík guesthouse or a packed meal from the resort.
meals.lunch: Café/snack bar near Jökulsárlón — there is a small café serving hot drinks, soup, and waffles at the lagoon car park (~2,000–3,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Hot meal at Systrakaffi in Kirkjubæjarklaustur on the drive back — try the Icelandic lamb burger or fish soup (~3,500–5,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 375 km from Reykjavik — this is a long driving day. Consider renting a comfortable 4WD SUV for these days. The glacier lagoon is open year-round and is stunning in winter with ice formations. Boat tours on the lagoon are not available in January due to ice, but the shoreline views are equally spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest day at the resort. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and use resort amenities. Take a gentle beachfront walk to decompress after the intensive driving days. Spend time in the resort spa or hot tub if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon visit to a local geothermal swimming pool (sundlaug) near the resort or in Reykjavik — Icelanders swim year-round in outdoor heated pools. Try the Laugardalslaug pool in Reykjavik (one of the largest) or a smaller local pool. Soak in the hot pots (hot tubs) alongside locals — a deeply authentic Icelandic cultural experience for only ~1,000 ISK entry.
day_by_day.evening: Casual evening in Reykjavik. Explore the bar and music scene on Laugavegur and Austurstræti streets. January evenings in Reykjavik are lively with locals. Enjoy live music at a pub or a quiet evening at a wine bar. Return to resort by taxi or arranged transfer.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or a nearby café — try Icelandic fish and chips.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Reykjavik at Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market) — excellent mid-range sushi and Icelandic seafood fusion (~5,000–7,000 ISK per person) or the more casual Reykjavik Fish Restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: This is an intentional recovery day. The previous two days of South Coast and glacier driving are physically demanding. Use today to recharge for the final stretch of the trip. The local swimming pool experience is one of Iceland's best-kept cultural secrets — don't miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike — note that full access to Landmannalaugar is typically limited in January due to snow and road conditions (F-roads are closed to all vehicles). However, a guided winter super jeep tour to the area may be available from specialized operators. If accessible, trek through the rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains and soak in the natural geothermal hot spring river at the end of the hike. If roads are closed, arrange an alternative guided hike in the Þórsmörk valley or a snowshoeing tour near Reykjavik instead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the hike/tour. Stop at a geothermal bakery in Laugarvatn — try the famous Laugarvatn Fontana geothermal bakery where rye bread is baked underground using geothermal steam for 24 hours. Take a dip in the Laugarvatn Fontana Spa (small lakeside geothermal spa, ~4,500 ISK) on the return route.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Quiet evening with dinner at the resort and early bedtime. Check aurora forecast for tomorrow night.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast before the guided tour departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail or provided by the tour operator — hot soup in a thermos is essential.
meals.dinner: Comfort dinner at the resort — opt for the heartiest menu item available, such as slow-cooked lamb or beef stew, to recover from the hike.

day_by_day.notes: IMPORTANT: Landmannalaugar F-roads (F208) are strictly closed in January. Only specially equipped super jeeps with experienced guides can attempt the route. Verify accessibility with your tour operator at least 48 hours in advance and have a backup plan ready. The Laugarvatn Fontana geothermal bread experience is a guaranteed highlight regardless of Landmannalaugar access.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Reykjanes Peninsula — explore the dramatic lava fields, geothermal areas, and coastline close to the resort. Visit Gunnuhver Hot Springs (powerful boiling mud pools and steam vents) and the Reykjanes Lighthouse on Iceland's southwestern tip. The area has seen recent volcanic activity — check with local authorities about safe access zones.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for final souvenir shopping on Laugavegur Street. Pick up Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), local chocolate, Brennivín schnapps, and handmade crafts. Visit the Kolaportið Flea Market (open weekends) for affordable local goods and vintage finds. Explore the Harpa Concert Hall — stunning geometric glass architecture on the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt — either join a third Super Jeep tour or self-drive to a pre-researched dark location near the resort. This is your last best opportunity for aurora viewing. Celebrate the trip with a special farewell dinner in Reykjavik.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Reykjavik food hall — try Hlemmur Mathöll (food hall) for diverse Icelandic street food options (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Dill Restaurant (Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant) or VOX Restaurant — splurge slightly for this final evening (~8,000–12,000 ISK per person for a memorable meal).

day_by_day.notes: Pack most of your luggage tonight to make tomorrow morning smooth. Keep aurora-watching gear (warm layers, camera, tripod) easily accessible for the evening. The Reykjanes Peninsula volcanic activity changes seasonally — always check icelandicvolcano.is for current conditions before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up and enjoy one last Icelandic breakfast at the resort. Take a slow final walk along the beachfront, breathe in the Arctic air, and soak in the memories. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. If your flight is in the afternoon or evening, consider a final stop at the Blue Lagoon (they offer a pre-flight package specifically designed for departing travelers — shower and luggage storage included) for one last geothermal soak before the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Keflavik International Airport (allow 45–60 minutes from the resort area). Check in for your departure flight. Browse the airport's Icelandic duty-free for last-minute gifts — Icelandic spirits, chocolates, and beauty products from the Blue Lagoon skincare line. Reflect on 13 incredible days of northern lights, hot springs, glaciers, and Icelandic culture.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland — carry the magic of the aurora, the warmth of the geothermal waters, and the wild beauty of the North Atlantic home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final full Icelandic breakfast at the resort — savor every bite.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Blue Lagoon pre-flight package café or at Keflavik Airport (~2,500–4,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport.

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Lagoon Pre-Flight Package must be booked in advance and is specifically designed for departing travelers — it includes towel, drink, and luggage storage. Arrive at Keflavik Airport at least 2.5 hours before international departure. January weather can occasionally cause flight delays — monitor your airline app. Ensure all Icelandic króna is spent or exchanged before departure as ISK has limited exchange value outside Iceland.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the aurora borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to maximize your viewing experience, often venturing to remote highland locations.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy the signature silica mud mask, in-water bar service, and steam caves while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for a well-rounded experience within budget.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and small geysers in a stunning rural setting, offering a more local and intimate experience.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and cultural landmarks on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs at iconic spots like Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church and the colorful old harbor district.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's breathtaking rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve and reward yourself with a soak in the natural geothermal hot spring pool at Landmannalaugar. The hike offers surreal landscapes of obsidian lava fields, steaming vents, and vivid multicolored mountains unlike anywhere else on Earth.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, settle into your beachfront suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity – a glass of Icelandic schnapps (Brennivín) and a light charcuterie board prepared by the resort. Freshen up and rest after the journey.

meals.breakfast: On board the flight
meals.lunch: On board the flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome charcuterie and cheese board with Brennivín schnapps provided by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance with the resort concierge. No activities scheduled before arrival. Keep Day 1 light – rest is essential for the days ahead. Confirm all upcoming bookings with the concierge before sleeping.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant overlooking the beachfront. Orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby coastline to acclimate to the Icelandic winter atmosphere. Visit the resort's private geothermal hot tub to soak away jet lag.
day_by_day.afternoon: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa: Just 20 minutes from the resort, indulge in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters. Book the premium 'Retreat' package, which includes access to the exclusive Retreat Spa, private changing suite, in-water massages, and a silica mud mask ritual. Spend 3–4 hours luxuriating in the mineral-rich waters.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the Blue Lagoon's LAVA Restaurant, perched on the edge of the lava field with panoramic views of the lagoon. Enjoy a tasting menu featuring Icelandic langoustine, Arctic char, and skyr-based desserts paired with Icelandic craft beer or a curated wine flight. Return to resort for an early night.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast buffet at the resort's signature restaurant – skyr, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Light in-water lagoon refreshments at the Blue Lagoon Retreat lounge – sparkling wine, fresh fruit, and Icelandic flatbreads
meals.dinner: LAVA Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon – premium Icelandic tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Blue Lagoon Retreat package well in advance as it sells out quickly, especially in January. January sunset is around 16:30, so afternoon lighting will be dramatic and atmospheric. Bring a hair tie – silica can be harsh on hair.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour: Private guided tour through Reykjavik's vibrant culinary and cultural scene. Sample traditional Icelandic delicacies including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, lamb soup, and fresh pastries from artisan bakeries. Visit iconic landmarks including Hallgrímskirkja Church, Harpa Concert Hall, and the old harbor district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavik independently at leisure. Browse the boutiques on Laugavegur Street for premium Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa) and local design. Visit the National Museum of Iceland for a deep dive into Viking history and Icelandic heritage. Stop at Reykjavik Art Museum (Kjarvalsstaðir) for rotating contemporary exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Dill Restaurant, Iceland's first and only Michelin-starred restaurant. Experience New Nordic cuisine that celebrates local, foraged, and seasonal Icelandic ingredients – expect dishes like smoked lamb, wild herbs, and preserved Arctic berries. Reserve the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing for the full experience.

meals.breakfast: Artisan breakfast at Brauð & Co bakery in Reykjavik – fresh sourdough, cinnamon rolls, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Tasting stops included in the Food & Culture Walking Tour – a curated selection of local delicacies across multiple vendors
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant – Michelin-starred New Nordic tasting menu with Icelandic wine and spirits pairing

day_by_day.notes: Private luxury transfer to/from Reykjavik (approx. 45 minutes from resort). Dill requires reservations made weeks or months in advance – confirm before the trip. January days are short (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~16:00), so plan outdoor sightseeing in the afternoon window.

day_by_day.morning: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep (Morning Preparation): Begin the day with a late, leisurely breakfast at the resort. Meet your expert guide and review the evening's aurora forecast. Spend the morning at the resort's spa facilities, including the geothermal pool and steam room, to relax before the night ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private helicopter tour over the Reykjanes Peninsula lava fields and geothermal vents (arrange through resort concierge). Witness Iceland's volcanic landscape from above – steaming fissures, black lava fields, and the dramatic coastline. Land near a remote geothermal area for a champagne toast before returning.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep: Board a custom-built super jeep with your expert aurora guide. Travel deep into the Icelandic highlands away from all light pollution. The guide will use real-time aurora forecasts and cloud cover maps to position you perfectly. Enjoy hot chocolate and Icelandic lamb soup served from a thermos while waiting for the aurora borealis to dance overhead. Photography assistance provided.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely à la carte breakfast at the resort – Icelandic pancakes with crowberry jam, smoked lamb, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Private in-room dining at the resort – lobster bisque, open-faced shrimp sandwiches, and Icelandic flatbread
meals.dinner: Hearty Icelandic lamb soup and hot chocolate provided during the Northern Lights tour; late-night return to resort with a warm nightcap at the bar

day_by_day.notes: January is peak aurora season in Iceland with up to 18 hours of darkness. The KP index should be monitored daily – your guide will have the latest data. Dress in extreme cold-weather layers; the resort concierge can provide premium thermal gear if needed. The super jeep tour typically runs from 21:00–01:00.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the late-night aurora hunt. Sleep in and enjoy a late breakfast delivered to your suite via in-room dining. Spend time in the resort's private infinity hot tub overlooking the Atlantic Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak: Private transfer to Flúðir village (approximately 1.5 hours from the resort). Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891 – a naturally heated geothermal pool set in a dramatic landscape of steaming geysers and bubbling hot springs. Far more intimate and authentic than the Blue Lagoon, with far fewer crowds. Arrange a private session for an exclusive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Friðheimar – a unique greenhouse restaurant in Reykholt where tomatoes are grown year-round using geothermal energy. The menu centers entirely around fresh tomatoes in creative preparations: tomato soup, tomato-based cocktails, and hearty mains. A truly one-of-a-kind Icelandic dining experience. Return to resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: In-room dining – smoked salmon eggs Benedict, fresh fruit plate, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic basket from the resort enjoyed near the Secret Lagoon – Icelandic cheeses, smoked meats, rye bread, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Friðheimar greenhouse restaurant – tomato tasting menu with tomato-based Bloody Mary cocktails and locally sourced accompaniments

day_by_day.notes: Book a private session at the Secret Lagoon through the resort concierge for an exclusive experience. Friðheimar requires advance reservations. The drive through the Golden Circle area offers stunning winter landscapes – request a scenic route from your driver.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle Private Tour (Part 1): Depart early by private luxury vehicle for the iconic Golden Circle route. First stop: Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park – a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk through the dramatic rift valley and learn about Iceland's Viking parliament heritage with your private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Golden Circle Private Tour (Part 2): Visit the Geysir Geothermal Area to witness Strokkur geyser erupting every 5–10 minutes, shooting boiling water up to 30 meters high. Continue to Gullfoss Waterfall – Iceland's most powerful waterfall, dramatically frozen and iced over in January. Enjoy the ethereal winter landscape with mist rising from the falls.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort via the Kerið volcanic crater lake – a 6,500-year-old crater with vivid red, black, and white volcanic rock surrounding a deep blue-green lake. Arrive back at resort for a private dinner in your suite – a curated five-course meal prepared by the resort's executive chef featuring the finest Icelandic ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the resort before departure – fresh pastries, cold cuts, skyr, and coffee
meals.lunch: Premium packed lunch enjoyed at Gullfoss – thermos of lobster bisque, smoked lamb sandwiches, Icelandic chocolates, and hot tea
meals.dinner: Private in-suite five-course dinner prepared by the resort's executive chef – Icelandic langoustine, pan-seared Arctic char, lamb tenderloin, artisan cheese board, and skyr panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: January roads on the Golden Circle are generally well-maintained but can be icy – ensure your private driver has a 4WD vehicle. Sunrise is around 11:00 and sunset around 16:30, so plan to be at the most photogenic locations during this golden hour window. Dress in multiple thermal layers.

day_by_day.morning: Spa and Wellness Day at the Resort: Full morning dedicated to the resort's premium spa facilities. Begin with a traditional Icelandic steam bath (sauna) followed by a hot-cold contrast therapy session. Book a 90-minute volcanic stone massage using local basalt stones heated in geothermal water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snæfellsnes Peninsula Private Day Tour (Part 1): Private transfer northwest toward the mystical Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park, home to the glacier that Jules Verne used as the entry point to the Earth's core in 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Explore the dramatic lava fields of Berserkjahraun and the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi.
day_by_day.evening: Continue along Snæfellsnes to Kirkjufell Mountain – Iceland's most photographed peak – and its adjacent waterfall, Kirkjufellsfoss. In January, the combination of potential aurora activity above the iconic mountain and the frozen waterfall creates one of Iceland's most magical photography opportunities. Enjoy a private aurora watch here before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Spa breakfast at the resort wellness center – açaí bowls, fresh smoothies, poached eggs, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Lunch at Fjöruhúsið café in Hellnar – a cozy cliffside café serving homemade fish soup, freshly baked bread, and Icelandic cakes with ocean views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Búðir's restaurant – one of Iceland's most acclaimed rural restaurants, serving locally sourced lamb, fresh fish, and seasonal ingredients in an intimate, candlelit setting

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Snæfellsnes is approximately 2–2.5 hours each way. January weather on the peninsula can be unpredictable – pack waterproof outer layers. Kirkjufell is best visited at dusk for aurora potential. Book Hotel Búðir dinner in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike (Preparation): Note that Landmannalaugar is only accessible by super jeep in winter. Depart early with a private super jeep and expert mountain guide. The journey itself is an adventure through snow-covered lava fields and river crossings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike: Arrive at the geothermal wonderland of Landmannalaugar in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve. Trek through Iceland's extraordinary rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains – vivid shades of red, orange, yellow, green, and purple – set against snow-white winter landscapes. Soak in the natural hot spring pool where geothermal water meets cool mountain streams, creating the perfect bathing temperature.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey through the highlands as darkness falls – keep eyes open for aurora activity on the drive back. Arrive at the resort for a late dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant. Enjoy a celebratory meal with a bottle of premium Champagne to mark the halfway point of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at the resort – scrambled eggs, Icelandic lamb sausages, rye bread with butter, and strong coffee before the long day
meals.lunch: Premium packed lunch in the Landmannalaugar hut – hot lamb stew from a thermos, rye bread, Icelandic chocolate, dried fruits, and nuts
meals.dinner: Resort fine dining restaurant – premium tasting menu with Champagne and wine pairing; Icelandic langoustine bisque, slow-roasted lamb, and volcanic salt caramel dessert

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar in January requires a specialized super jeep with experienced highland guides – this is non-negotiable for safety. The hot spring soak mid-hike is extraordinary in winter with snow surrounding the pool. Bring a dry bag for towels and a change of clothes. This is a full-day excursion (10–12 hours).

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the demanding Landmannalaugar day. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely in-room breakfast, and spend time reading or relaxing in the resort's lounge with floor-to-ceiling ocean views. Optional: gentle yoga session with the resort's private instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: South Coast Private Tour: Private luxury vehicle heads east along Iceland's dramatic South Coast. Visit Seljalandsfoss waterfall – in January, the falls are dramatically iced with frozen curtains of ice. Walk behind the waterfall (conditions permitting) for a unique perspective. Continue to Skógafoss waterfall, where ice formations create a cathedral-like frozen landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Continue to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara – one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt columns and powerful Atlantic waves. Watch the sun set (around 16:30) over the basalt sea stacks of Reynisdrangar. Dinner at Hótel Rangá – one of Iceland's finest rural hotels, with a renowned restaurant serving Arctic char, reindeer, and Icelandic lamb. Return to resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: In-room dining – smoked salmon bagel, fresh fruit salad, skyr with Icelandic honey, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Stop at Skál! restaurant in Vík – a cozy spot serving freshly made lamb burgers, fish and chips, and Icelandic soups with local bread
meals.dinner: Hótel Rangá restaurant – Nordic fine dining with reindeer carpaccio, pan-seared Arctic char, and Icelandic lamb rack with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves – stay well back from the water's edge regardless of conditions. The South Coast roads are generally good in January but check conditions. Hótel Rangá is also an excellent aurora-watching location and has its own aurora wake-up service.

day_by_day.morning: Private Ice Cave Tour: Depart early by private super jeep for Vatnajökull glacier – Europe's largest glacier. Meet your certified glacier guide for an exclusive private ice cave tour. The natural ice caves beneath Vatnajökull form only in winter and are accessible from November to March. The caves glow in extraordinary shades of blue, teal, and black.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the glacier experience with a private glacier walk on Sólheimajökull glacier outlet. Equipped with crampons, ice axes, and helmets, explore the glacier's crevasses, ice formations, and ash layers from past volcanic eruptions with your expert guide. This is an intimate, exclusive experience arranged for your group only.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort as darkness falls. Second Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep: Your guide will have monitored the KP index throughout the day. If conditions are favorable (clear skies and high aurora activity), embark on a second dedicated aurora hunt from a different location, potentially near the volcanic highlands for dramatic foreground compositions.

meals.breakfast: Early energy-packed breakfast at the resort – oatmeal with Icelandic berries, protein-rich eggs, smoked lamb, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch enjoyed in a sheltered spot near the glacier – lamb stew in a thermos, artisan sandwiches, and hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the resort's bar and grill – Icelandic beef burger with truffle fries, local craft beers, and a warming dessert of warm skyr cake with bilberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Ice caves are natural formations and their accessibility depends on conditions – your guide will confirm the day before. This is a physically active day; ensure appropriate footwear and cold-weather gear. The combination of ice cave and aurora in one day is one of Iceland's ultimate luxury experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort spa day. Begin with a private geothermal pool session at the resort. Book a luxury 'Iceland Ritual' treatment: a full-body volcanic mud wrap using locally sourced geothermal minerals, followed by a deep-tissue massage with Icelandic birch oil. Spend the morning in complete relaxation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reykjavik Luxury Shopping & Culture: Private transfer to Reykjavik for an afternoon of premium shopping and cultural exploration. Visit Kolaportið flea market for authentic Icelandic souvenirs and vintage finds. Browse luxury boutiques on Skólavörðustígur for high-end Icelandic design, jewelry, and woolen goods. Visit the Icelandic Phallological Museum for a uniquely Icelandic cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-approaching dinner at Óx – Reykjavik's most exclusive and intimate restaurant. With only 12 seats and a single communal table, Óx offers a theatrical 20-course tasting experience celebrating Icelandic ingredients. Reservations are extremely limited and must be secured months in advance. This is a once-in-a-lifetime dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Spa wellness breakfast at the resort – green smoothies, avocado toast on rye, poached eggs, and herbal infusions
meals.lunch: Lunch at Messinn in Reykjavik – renowned for their cast-iron skillets of fresh Icelandic fish served with butter, herbs, and rye bread
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant – 20-course theatrical tasting menu with full beverage pairing including Icelandic spirits, natural wines, and craft beers

day_by_day.notes: Óx reservations must be made months in advance – this should be one of the first bookings made when planning the trip. The experience lasts approximately 3–4 hours. Private transfer back to the resort after dinner. This is the culinary highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Whale Watching & Arctic Wildlife Tour: Depart from Reykjavik's old harbor on a private luxury whale-watching vessel. January offers opportunities to spot humpback whales, minke whales, white-beaked dolphins, and harbor porpoises in the cold Faxaflói Bay. The vessel is equipped with heated indoor viewing areas and premium amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan Museum in Reykjavik – a stunning glass dome structure built atop geothermal hot water tanks. Explore the 'Wonders of Iceland' exhibition featuring a real indoor ice cave, aurora simulator, and immersive volcanic experience. Enjoy panoramic 360-degree views over Reykjavik from the observation deck.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt: Return to the resort and monitor aurora conditions. If forecasts are favorable, embark on one final private aurora hunt with your guide to a specially selected location. If aurora conditions are poor, enjoy a private stargazing session with a telescope on the resort grounds, followed by a nightcap of Icelandic Brennivín and local craft spirits at the resort bar.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast at the resort before the whale watching departure – smoked fish, rye bread, skyr, fresh pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Premium lunch on board the whale-watching vessel – hot Icelandic fish soup, open-faced sandwiches, and hot drinks served with ocean views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Grillið restaurant atop the Radisson Blu Saga Hotel in Reykjavik – panoramic rooftop fine dining with Icelandic lamb, Arctic char, and an extensive wine cellar; spectacular city views

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January has a high success rate for humpback whales. Book a private charter for the most exclusive experience. Dress in extreme cold-weather gear for the deck. The Perlan Museum is excellent for understanding Iceland's geological and natural phenomena – great context for the whole trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the resort. Wake up for one last soak in the resort's private geothermal hot tub as the winter sun rises around 11:00. Enjoy a long, leisurely farewell breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport. Allow extra time for a final stop at the Blue Lagoon's Retreat Spa for a 2-hour farewell soak and spa treatment before your flight (the Blue Lagoon is conveniently located near the airport – perfect for a pre-flight visit). Depart Iceland refreshed, relaxed, and unforgettable memories richer.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Enjoy the Icelandair or United Airlines premium lounge before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort – full Icelandic spread with smoked salmon, lamb, skyr, fresh pastries, eggs, and freshly squeezed juice; toast with Champagne to celebrate an extraordinary trip
meals.lunch: Final Blue Lagoon Retreat lounge refreshments – sparkling wine, Icelandic flatbreads, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or on-board premium cabin dining

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time and work backward to plan the Blue Lagoon stop – allow at least 3 hours at the lagoon plus 30 minutes transfer to the airport. Pre-book the final Blue Lagoon visit. Purchase last-minute Icelandic souvenirs at the airport's duty-free: Icelandic wool, lava salt, Brennivín, and local chocolate. Request a late checkout from the resort if available.
